sets.title: Employment: Activity (downsizing)
sets.note: Labelled “Activity” on the slide. No task is written on the slide; the deck is titled “From English to Arabic”. The direction shown is an assumption for the instructor to confirm.

items.text: Downsizing is the intentional process of reducing the scale, size, or complexity of an organization or personal life to improve efficiency and reduce costs. In the corporate world, it often involves permanent workforce reductions and operational restructuring to keep a business financially viable during economic shifts. On a personal level, downsizing typically means moving to a smaller home and parting with excess belongings to embrace a simpler, more manageable lifestyle. Ultimately, whether applied to a multi-million dollar company or an individual household, the core objective of downsizing is the same: shedding unnecessary weight to create a more streamlined, agile, and sustainable path forward.

sets.title: Employment: Activity (employment systems)
sets.note: Labelled “Activity” on the slide. No task is written on the slide; the deck is titled “From English to Arabic”. The direction shown is an assumption for the instructor to confirm.

items.text: The centrality of labor flexibility, wage costs, and unemployment in debates over European economic development puts employment systems at the heart of any putative Europeanization of national economics. An employment system refers to the interaction of various formative institutions making up the national and sectoral profile of the labor force. These institutions making comprise the training and educational processes, the legal and industrial relations requlations, the organizational structure and practices of industry, and the politics of the workplace.

items.label: Costs of Downsizing
items.text: Downsizing is often very costly to a corporation. More than 50 percent of companies that downsize fall to reach their financial objectives. More than one million people are permanently laid off each year. For example, Boeing eleminated 60,000 jobs between 1989 and 1997. The company’s orders fofr jets icreased from two hundred to nine hundred within two years. The company had had a difficult time hiring qualified people.

items.label: Job Market
items.text: A number of measures were attempted in order to combat the crisis in the job market. Thus, employment measures and unemployment insurance were improved, as well as measures for those who had lost their jobs. The parliament adopted the “law for employment initiative.” The aim of the law is to mitigate the impact of the financial crisis on the unemployed, to create means by which job posititions can be maintained, and to give a larger number of people the opportunity to participate in employment activities.

items.label: UK and Redundancy
items.text:
Redundancy is a form of dismissal from your job. It happens when employers need to reduce their workforce.
If you’re being made redundant, you might be eligible for certain things, including:
redundancy pay
a notice period
a consultation with your employer
the option to move into a different job
time off to find a new job

sets.title: The Basics of Investing in Stocks
sets.note: The slide heading says Arabic to English, but the text is in English. The direction shown (English to Arabic) is an assumption for the instructor to confirm.

items.label: Slide 10
items.text:
The Basics of Investing In Stocks
What Are Stocks?
Stocks are a type of security that gives stockholders a share of ownership in a company.
Companies sell shares typically to gain additional money to grow the company. This is called the initial public offering (IPO). After the IPO, stockholders can resell shares on the stock market.
Stock prices rise or fall and are typically driven by expectations of the corporation’s earnings, or profits.

items.label: Slide 11
items.text:
Types Of Stocks
There are two main kinds of stocks, common stock and preferred stock.
Common Stocks
Common stock entitles owners to vote at shareholder meetings and receive dividends.
Preferred Stocks
Preferred stockholders usually don’t have voting rights but they receive dividend payments before common stockholders do, and have priority over common stockholders if the company goes bankrupt and its assets are liquidated.
Growth Stocks
Growth stocks have earnings growing at a faster rate than the market average. They rarely pay dividends and investors buy them in the hope of capital appreciation. A start-up technology company is likely to be a growth stock.

items.label: Slide 12
items.text:
Types Of Stocks
Income Stocks
Income stocks pay dividends consistently. Dividends are a portion of the company’s earnings paid to shareholders. Investors buy them for the income they generate. An established utility company is likely to be an income stock.
Value Stocks
Value stock shave a low price-to-earnings (PE) ratio, meaning they are cheaper to buy than stocks with a higher PE. Value stocks may be growth or income stocks, and their low PE ratio may reflect the fact that they have fallen out of favor with investors for some reason. People buy value stocks in the hope that the market has overreacted and that the stock’s price will rebound.
Blue-Chip Stocks
Blue-chip stocks are shares in large, well-known companies with a solid history of growth. They generally pay dividends.

items.label: Slide 13
items.text:
Potential Benefits Of Investing In Stocks
The potential benefits of investing in stocks include:
Potential capital gains from owning a stock that grows in value over time
Potential income from dividends paid by the company
Lower tax rates on long-term capital gains

items.label: Slide 14
items.text:
Potential Risks Of Stocks
The potential risks of investing in stocks include:
Share prices for a company falling, even to zero
If the company goes broke, you may be the last to be paid, so you may not get your money back
The value of your shares will go up and down, and the dividend may vary

items.text: The global financial landscape has transformed significantly with the rise of digital assets. Cryptocurrency trading, which involves buying and selling digital currencies to profit from short-term price fluctuations, has moved from a niche hobby into mainstream finance. Unlike traditional stock markets that operate within strict business hours, the cryptocurrency market is decentralized and runs twenty-four hours a day, seven days a week. This continuous accessibility offers unprecedented flexibility for traders, but it also demands constant vigilance.

reference.text: لقد شهد المشهد المالي العالمي تحولاً كبيراً مع صعود الأصول الرقمية. ولم يعد تداول العملات المشفرة —الذي ينطوي على شراء العملات الرقمية وبيعها للربح من تقلبات الأسعار قصيرة الأجل— مجرد هواية لفئة محدودة، بل انتقل إلى قلب القطاع المالي العام. وبخلاف أسواق الأسهم التقليدية التي تعمل ضمن ساعات عمل رسمية صارمة، فإن سوق العملات المشفرة يتسم باللامركزية، ويعمل على مدار الساعة طوال أيام الأسبوع. ويمنح هذا التوافر المستمر مرونة غير مسبوقة للمتداولين، لكنه يتطلب في الوقت نفسه يقظة دائمة.

items.text: To navigate this market successfully, participants must understand its core mechanisms. Traders typically use online platforms known as cryptocurrency exchanges to execute their orders. Transactions are carried out via trading pairs, such as Bitcoin against the US Dollar (BTC/USD.

reference.text: ولكي يتمكن المشاركون من دخول هذا السوق بنجاح، يتعين عليهم فهم آلياته الأساسية. وعادةً ما يستخدم المتداولون منصات عبر الإنترنت تُعرف باسم "بورصات العملات المشفرة" لتنفيذ أوامرهم. وتُجرى المعاملات من خلال "أزواج التداول"، مثل البيتكوين مقابل الدولار الأمريكي (BTC/USD).

items.text: However, the allure of high returns comes with substantial danger. Cryptocurrencies are notorious for their extreme volatility, meaning an asset's value can plummet or skyrocket within minutes based on regulatory news, technological updates, or social media speculation.

reference.text: ومع ذلك، فإن جاذبية العوائد المرتفعة تنطوي على مخاطر جسيمة؛ فالعملات المشفرة معروفة بتقلباتها الشديدة، مما يعني أن قيمة الأصل يمكن أن تنخفض أو ترتفع بشكل حاد في غضون دقائق بناءً على الأخبار التنظيمية، أو التحديثات التقنية، أو المضاربات عبر وسائل التواصل الاجتماعي

ساعات التداول:

reference.text:
Muscat Stock Exchange (MSX) Overview
The MSX is the official financial market for trading securities and equities (bonds and stocks) in the Sultanate of Oman.
Market History:
Established in June 1988 as the Muscat Securities Market.
Transformed into a closed joint-stock company (MSX) in 2021.
Trading Hours:
Official trading sessions start daily at 9:30 AM.
Main Indicator:
The MSX30 Index tracks the top 30 most liquid stocks.

items.label: Steps to start investing
items.text:
خطوات البدء والاستثمار
اختر وسيطاً مالياً:
التعامل يتم عبر شركات الوساطة المرخصة في السلطنة
فتح حساب تداول:
مراجعة شركة الوساطة لاستكمال مستندات التسجيل وفتح الحساب.
متابعة البيانات:
استخدام التطبيق الذكي أو الموقع الرسمي لمتابعة الأسعار لحظياً

reference.text:
Steps to Start Investing
Select a broker:
Trading requires an authorized brokerage firm in Oman.
Open an account:
Submit registration documents through your chosen broker.
Monitor data:
Use the official MSX app for real-time price updates.
